portInfo.description: Port of Québec operates two named cruise terminals plus additional wharves open to cruise ships. The Ross-Gaudreault Terminal serves Wharves 21 and 22 beside Old Québec; Cruise Terminal 30 (built 2020, passenger ramp 2021) is designed for large ships and both port-of-call and embark/disembark operations. Official passenger-access pages publish street addresses and geographic coordinates for Pointe-à-Carcy, Estuaire Quai 30 and Lévis Quai 81. Other wharves listed as open to cruise ships include Coast Guard Wharf 93 — passenger frequency there is Not verified. Always confirm which wharf appears on the day’s Port of Québec schedule.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Old Québec / Petit-Champlain — adjacent framing from Ross-Gaudreault — ~150 min.
Château Frontenac / Dufferin Terrace — uphill; buffer for hills.
Musée de la civilisation — Lower Town; hours Not verified.
Montmorency Falls — organised only; transfer Not verified.
Lévis waterfront — only if berthed at Quai 81.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Check whether you are at Pointe-à-Carcy, Estuaire 30 or Lévis 81 before planning a “walk to the Château” day — only Pointe-à-Carcy is framed as Old Québec-adjacent.
